thread:
raj: getting flood of alerts from nodes in us-west-2a, ephemeral storage at 98% on two nodes. a few model-serving pods got OOM/killed and then restarted constantly. paging oncall now.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: ephemeral-storage-critical — paging @oncall (severity: p0) — reason: node ephemeral storage saturation, repeated pod terminations. link: https://redwood.inc/incident/1923456789

emily: seeing repeated messages in kubelet logs: 
```
Kubelet: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage: threshold reached
Pod "model-serve-xyz" evicted: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage
runtime: cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: failed to allocate workspace
```

emily: pod logs show the serving runtime crashed with CUDA alloc errors immediately after cache warmup. suspect model cache writes to tmpfs/emptyDir filling up along with debug logs.

maria: copying some quick outputs — `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` shows restart loops on model-serve-* across node-5 and node-7. kubelet events show `DiskPressure` then `Evicted`.

sam: root cause hypothesis: model cache writes + verbose debug logs + system journal + other tenant workloads saturated ephemeral storage (emptyDir/tmpfs). when kubelet evicted pods, the runtime couldn't recover (cuda workspace alloc fails because container restarted with corrupted cache or insufficient free space).

emily: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) scale down cache-populators and noncritical workers 2) rotate/delete oldest logs on the affected nodes 3) cordon one node and run cleanup 4) restart model-serving pods after cleanup.

maria: doing steps 2-3 now. running on node-5:
```bash
ssh root@node-5
# find and truncate large logs older than 7d
find /var/log -type f -mtime +7 -exec truncate -s 0 {} \; 2>/dev/null
# clear model cache temp dir (model runtime uses /var/tmp/model-cache)
rm -rf /var/tmp/model-cache/* || true
# free system journal
journalctl --vacuum-time=2d || true
```

raj: @maria please be careful with rm -rf — only target known runtime cache dirs. we don't want to delete host-level data.

maria: acknowledged. running with explicit paths. cleaning /var/tmp/model-cache and old rotated logs. freeing ~45GB on node-5 so far.

sam: I'll scale down the cache prefetch job in k8s to 0 replicas: `kubectl scale deploy/cache-prefetch -n inference --replicas=0`

emily: scaled noncritical workloads down. deploy-bot: confirmed rollback of prefetcher to 0.

deploy-bot: deploy status: cache-prefetch scaled -> 0 (success)

emily: cordoned node-7 and draining non-daemon pods that can be rescheduled off it to prevent further evictions: `kubectl cordon node-7` `kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30`

julian-cs: customer-impact: monitoring shows two customers with requests getting 5xx during the incident window (~12:21-12:38 UTC). added to incident ticket. I'll notify their CS reps.

raj: good. next: we need to restart the model-serving pods gracefully once nodes report free space. make sure runtime starts with `--cache-mode=readonly` to avoid heavy writes on restart. can we patch the deployment?

emily: we can patch deployment with env override: `kubectl set env deploy/model-serve --namespace=inference CACHE_MODE=readonly` and then rollout restart. planning to do a canary 1/5 on node-3 first.

maria: node-5 is stable, free space back to 70%. rerunning `kubectl get pods -n inference` shows model-serve on node-3 recovered, node-7 still flapping.

sre_lead: handoff — I need to step in for follow-up. @maria you're primary on remediation, @raj you own customer comms, @julian-cs keep tracking impacted customers.

maria: performing controlled rollout: set CACHE_MODE=readonly, reduce log level to info, set env LOG_MAX_SIZE=10M. commands: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-serve CACHE_MODE=readonly LOG_LEVEL=info LOG_MAX_SIZE=10M
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-serve --watch
```

emily: applying patch now. starting canary (1/5). monitoring memory and disk.

10m later...

emily: canary stable. no new evictions on node-3. proceeding with rolling restart.

sam: once restarts complete, we should redeploy a job to periodically scrub `/var/tmp/model-cache` and add logrotate for runtime logs. also add a node-level crontab to vacuum journal more aggressively.

raj: customer update draft: "We experienced transient errors during 12:20-12:40 UTC due to ephemeral storage saturation on a subset of nodes which caused model-serving restarts. We have restored service and are applying mitigations; investigating root cause and will follow up with permanent mitigations." @julian-cs please send.

julian-cs: sent to affected customers. one asked for SLA credit; I've opened a support case.

sre_lead: post-incident action items (captured here):
- Add alert to track free ephemeral-storage per node with 10% headroom.
- Implement logrotate + limit runtime log size via container config.
- Add model-cache eviction policy and cap per-pod disk usage (emptyDir size or hostPath quotas).
- Re-evaluate prefetcher resource requests & limits; avoid aggressive warmups.
- Provision larger ephemeral volumes in us-west-2a (capacity planning).
- Run a chaos test to validate eviction/fallback behavior for model-serving.

maria: creating follow-up ticket: INF-3542 - "Ephemeral storage saturation causes model cache + logs to induce pod restarts" with remediation steps.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, nodes stabilized, services recovering. incident severity degraded to P2.

raj: wrapping handoff. I'll monitor for 30m then close the incident if no regressions. thanks all. :thumbsup:

emily: adding runbook note: when ephemeral storage > 85% on any node, auto-scale down prefetcher and trigger cleanup job.

maria: last check: node-5/7 free space >65%, no more OOM/CUDA errors in pod logs.

sre_lead: closing note: keep INF-3542 assigned to infra-sre. we'll schedule a retro in next oncall sync.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 1923456789 — resolved by team at 1923457401.

raj: thanks everyone.
